message.content:
Let the projection of \(\mathbf{a}\) onto the plane \(P\) be
\[
\mathbf{x}=p\mathbf{b}+q\mathbf{c}.
\]
Since \(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{x}\) is perpendicular to \(P\), it is perpendicular to both \(\mathbf{b}\) and \(\mathbf{c}\). Thus
\[
\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=\frac15,
\]
\[
\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{c}=\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{c}=\frac16.
\]
Now
\[
\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{b}
= (p\mathbf{b}+q\mathbf{c})\cdot \mathbf{b}
= p+q(\mathbf{b}\cdot \mathbf{c})
= p+\frac q2,
\]
so
\[
p+\frac q2=\frac15.
\]
Similarly,
\[
\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{c}
= p(\mathbf{b}\cdot \mathbf{c})+q
= \frac p2+q=\frac16.
\]
So we solve
\[
\begin{cases}
p+\frac q2=\frac15,\\[4pt]
\frac p2+q=\frac16.
\end{cases}
\]
Multiplying the first equation by \(2\):
\[
2p+q=\frac25.
\]
Multiplying the second by \(2\):
\[
p+2q=\frac13.
\]
Solving gives
\[
p=\frac{7}{45},\qquad q=\frac{4}{45}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
(p,q)=\left(\frac{7}{45},\frac{4}{45}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\left(\frac{7}{45},\frac{4}{45}\right)\).
